topic: What happens if you sleep on top of Everest?
title: Night On Everest
hook: Could you survive one night on Everest?

beats.label: 1 HOUR
beats.line: Up here, every breath holds about a third of the oxygen at sea level.

beats.label: 3 HOURS
beats.line: Your heart races to push what little oxygen you have around your body.

beats.label: 6 HOURS
beats.line: Sleep turns choppy, and your breathing stops and starts all night.

beats.label: 12 HOURS
beats.line: Your brain can start to swell, causing headaches and confusion.

beats.label: 1 DAY
beats.line: Climbers call this the death zone: the body can't adapt, it only declines.

end.line: Would you spend a night up there?

description: Thin air, a racing heart and a swelling brain: one night on the roof of the world.

facts.claim: Air pressure on the summit of Everest is about one third of sea level, so each breath holds about a third of the oxygen.
facts.source: Britannica - Mount Everest; NIH - High altitude physiology

facts.claim: Heart rate rises at high altitude to compensate for low oxygen.
Periodic breathing (breathing that stops and starts) is common during sleep at high altitude.
facts.source: NIH / NCBI - Sleep at high altitude

facts.claim: High altitude cerebral edema is swelling of the brain causing headache and confusion.
Above about 8,000 m is called the death zone, where the body cannot acclimatize and deteriorates.
